learning_outcomes.text: Represent information in a format that can be processed by a computer.
Manipulate logical expressions and functions, minimize them through algebraic and Karnaugh-maps optimization method, and translate high-level functional specifications in the form of logic functions.
Design a combinational logic circuit, understand the basic architectures of binary adders, and have familiarity with the concept of performance optimization through appropriate architectural choices.
Translate an abstract problem of medium complexity into the formulation of a finite state machine. Synthesize a realization in the form of a combination of logic gates and registers.
Understand the main dynamic limitations of a medium complexity digital system.
Understand the concept abstraction level and represent medium-complex systems as a combination of subsystems of lower complexity.
Describe digital systems in VHDL, describe a system at different abstraction levels and organize the description of complex systems in various hierarchical levels.
Understand the organization and the main functions of a computing architecture.
Identify potentials and limits of a given type of memory, depending on the application context.
Apply priority techniques and communication protocols in the management of shared resources.
Describe the instruction flow within a computer.
Evaluate the different approaches for the management of asynchronous events in computers.

syllabus_topics: Analog and digital signals
Binary digital systems
Block diagram of a computer and a microcomputer
Description of the abstraction levels in the design of a digital system
Design flow
Binary representation of numerical and non-numerical information
Boolean algebra: properties and fundamental theorems
Concept of logic operator and logic gate
Difference between ideal and real logic gate
Normal forms
Minimization of two-level logic functions with the use of Karnaugh maps
Design of combinational logic: basic combinational blocks and hierarchical system design
Arithmetic blocks, binary adders and subtractors
Concept of sequential system, state variables and representation as a combination of combinatorial system and memory elements
Latches and flip-flops
Analysis and synthesis of a finite state machine
Basic elements of temporization and main dynamic limits of a sequential system
Overview of the implementation technologies for digital systems and programmable logic devices
Memory basics
Registers
Register transfers
Digital systems partitioned in control unit and datapath
Microoperations and register transfer language
Shift registers and counters
VHDL language for the representation (at different abstraction levels) and logic simulation of digital systems
Organization of a computer: datapath, memory, control unit, arithmetic-logical unit, input/output devices
Computer architecture: machine instructions, addressing methods, calls to subroutines, dynamic memory allocation
Memory organization: cache memory, virtual memory, memory mapping, and management unit (MMU)
Direct memory access (DMA)
Interruption systems: context switching, acknowledgment of outages, external interruptions, and software
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes, wooclap)
Use of tools for the logic simulation of digital systems using VHDL language
assessment_rules: The final exam consists of a written test. Attending students may earn up to +3 bonus points based on active participation. Assessment is based on the knowledge and understanding of concepts and methodologies, and the ability to apply them to solve specific problems. Evaluation criteria include accuracy and completeness of answers. Use of Generative AI Tools is not permitted during the exam.

Peter J. Ashenden, “The Designer’s Guide to VHDL” – Morgan Kaufmann, 2002, 2nd ed.
